precepts.text: Who was God warning? Solomon. What was Solomon's problem beyond the sin itself? Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. He could not take correction; nobody could tell him anything. From that flowed all his other problems. Even Solomon at the end understood the whole duty of man: fear God and keep his commandments. But he should not have had to go through it, with all the wisdom given to him and his father's life before his eyes.
precepts.point: But if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes: definition read in class, forsake means to abandon, desert, or leave entirely, a breach of duty. Then will I pluck them up by the roots, and make them to be a proverb and a byword among all nations. Reading that is understanding why we went into captivity.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Who was the Lord talking to in 2 Chronicles 7? Solomon. “if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked”, and “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes”, then “will I pluck them up by the roots”. So what was Solomon's problem, outside of the sin itself? Solomon tells it on himself: “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.”

That was his problem. He couldn't take correction. He didn't want to hear it; nobody could tell him nothing. That's like some brothers here: they can't be told, they don't want to hear it, they get offended. He was an old, foolish king who could no longer be admonished, and from that trickled all the other problems he had.

Even Solomon at the end understood the whole duty of man: to fear God and keep his commandments. But he shouldn't have had to go through that. All wisdom was given to him, and he saw his father's life before his eyes. He was concerned with how the world operated and wanted to experience the world, when we are supposed to be unspotted from this world.

So the forsaking that brought the captivity began with a king who could not be admonished. When you keep repeating something to people who can't be told anything, after a while you lose them. That is why we have to be willing to receive correction.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
precepts.point: Solomon praised the dead more than the living; Job wished he had died from the womb. The comfort is in the scriptures.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power”. That's us. Our oppressors have power: they organize themselves, pass laws and policies, colonize, oppress and exploit. And the Israelites had no comforter.

So what is supposed to comfort us? Paul says: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Whatsoever was written aforetime means this Bible, and it was written for our learning. We ought to learn from what happened to the Israelites, to the apostles, and to Christ.

“comfort of the scriptures”: this is our comforter. The scriptures of this Bible are where the oppressed find comfort, and that is what we need to hope in.

The oppressors hold all the cards right now, and the one who has no comforter in the world has one in the word. If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, the nations would have swallowed us up; it is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed.

precepts.text: Why died I not from the womb?
precepts.point: Solomon praised the dead more than the living; Job wished he had died from the womb. The comfort is in the scriptures.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
Because of verse 1, with no comforter and all the power on the side of our oppressors, Solomon says: “Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.” Better than both is he “which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.” He would rather praise the dead, who are not going through the oppression, than the living, who are depressed, oppressed, suppressed, pressed all kinds of ways.

Job said the same: “Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?” Job was going through tribulation hell: his wife on him, his kids dying, the skin disease, his lands, everything lost. Why didn't I just die already? Why am I still here?

“For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest”. If he had slept, meaning been dead, he would have been at rest, not going through the hell he was going through; or as “infants which never saw light”, meaning stillborn. “There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest. There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.” We are the prisoners. In death they don't have to deal with oppressors no more.

That is how heavy the oppression of Ecclesiastes 4:1 is. And the only reason we are still breathing is the mercy of the Lord, who has not given us as a prey to their teeth.

precepts.text: Two are better than one, and if two lie together they have heat, which is exactly what David's servants sought for him.
precepts.point: Abishag the Shunammite is found and ministers to the king, but he does not know her. That means he did not have relations with her; she was there only to keep him warm.

note.label: 1 Kings 1: A King Exalts Himself and a King Is Anointed

precepts.why:
“Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.” “Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?”

That is exactly what David's servants sought for him. King David “was old and stricken in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he gat no heat.” This is one of the things that happens with age, when the body no longer produces heat as it did in youth and strength. So they sought a young virgin, “and let her lie in thy bosom, that my lord the king may get heat.”

Abishag the Shunammite was found, and she “cherished the king, and ministered to him: but the king knew her not.” That means he did not have relations with her. She was there only to keep him warm.

precepts.text: Better is a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king who will no more be admonished, the very lesson of these young kings.
precepts.point: In the eighth year of his reign, while yet young, he begins to seek after the God of David, and in the twelfth year he begins to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, groves, and images.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
“Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.” That is the very lesson of these young kings.

Compare the ages. Manasseh began at twelve, Amon at twenty two, and Josiah “was eight years old when he began to reign”, yet the youngest was the wisest. Josiah “did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the ways of David his father”.

“For in the eighth year of his reign, while he was yet young, he began to seek after the God of David his father: and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, and the groves, and the carved images, and the molten images.” The wise child sought the Most High while the older kings before him would no more be admonished.

precepts.text: On the side of the oppressor there was power, but the oppressed had no comforter, which came to pass in the Babylonian captivity.
precepts.point: She weeps because the comforter that should relieve her soul is far from her; there was oppression but no comforter to relieve them.

note.label: Lamentations 1: The City That Sits Solitary

precepts.why:
Jerusalem weeps “because the comforter that should relieve my soul is far from me.” Solomon saw that condition: “So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.”

On the side of the oppressor there was power, but the oppressed had no comforter. That came to pass in the Babylonian captivity: the Most High trod under foot all her mighty men, called an assembly to crush her young men, the leaders taken out first, and delivered her into the hands of those from whom she could not rise up. There was oppression, but no comforter to relieve them.

moments.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

points: And behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter. And on the side of their oppressors — this does not say on the side of the police force, on the side of the judges, on the side of the medical examiner. No, it says on the side of your oppressors.

This is why Karen is so quick to say, I'll call the police. Because they know there's power on their side. Y'all understand that, right? Because they know that back in the day they had to call Billy Bob and the lynch mob was on their way. It's no different today. It is no different today.
And on the side of their oppressors there was power, but they had no comforter. It says but they had no comforter. On the side of the oppressor there was power.

So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: this is King Solomon speaking prophetically. And behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter: looking for justice in all the wrong places.
And on the side of their oppressors there was power: they have the weapons, the court system, all of it. We have nothing. But they had no comforter.

Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. When we work together, there is reward. The more of us there are, the more we can do. They are looking at us crazy right now because somehow we inhabited a ship with hundreds of people and took the gospel to about eight different countries without asking anybody's permission. Because we work together, collectively we are strong.

Woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up. The Deacon knew what it was like to be alone here in 2006, before anybody: he had to leave and go where two are better than one and get built up. There is strength in numbers: we hold each other accountable, support each other, and look after each other, if we truly love the Lord. But if we come into this thing like Hellenized Jews, the numbers will not profit us.
Behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; on the side of their oppressors there was power.
Solomon praised the dead more than the living; Job wished he had died from the womb. The comfort is in the scriptures.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

points: Solomon considers the oppressions done under the sun, the tears of the oppressed who had no comforter, and power on the side of their oppressors.
He praises the dead already dead more than the living, and better than both is he who has not yet been and has not seen the evil work done under the sun.

Solomon sees that for every right work a man is envied by his neighbor, and this too is vanity. Even envy is vanity, because the person you envy is going to die and lose their stuff just like you, so you are envying them for nothing.
The fool folds his hands and eats his own flesh, and better is a handful with quietness than both hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.

There is one alone with neither child nor brother, yet no end to his labor, and his eyes are never satisfied with riches; he never asks for whom he labors and bereaves his soul of good. This too is vanity and a sore travail.
Two are better than one, for they have a good reward for their labor; if they fall, one lifts up his fellow, but woe to him that is alone when he falls with no one to help him up.

A threefold cord is not quickly broken. This speaks of gathering together; you cannot call yourself an Israelite living alone. If you want the kingdom with everybody else but want to be alone in this life, that does not work, because when someone comes against you, you have no backup and nobody to help you.
Better is a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king who will no more be admonished, for out of prison the poor one comes to reign while the one born in the kingdom becomes poor.

Solomon considers all the living who walk under the sun and the child that shall stand up in the king's place; there is no end of all the people, yet those who come after shall not rejoice in him, and this too is vanity.
When it says there is no end of all the people, you cannot use that line to say our people were killed off throughout their day and are no longer around; they are still around.
